metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Texas (2026): Rules, Exemptions & Ex.

description: Texas has a statewide sales tax, but qualifying precious-metal bullion and many legal-tender coins are exempt; jewelry and medallions are taxed. Statewide rule.

What's covered by the exemption
Precious-metal bullion and many coins
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Texas.
Is gold and silver bullion taxable in Texas?
+
No, if it qualifies under Texas’s bullion/coin exemption. Qualifying precious-metal bullion is exempt from sales tax.
Are legal-tender coins exempt from sales tax in Texas?
+
Many are. Texas generally exempts many coins that qualify as legal tender or bullion under the administrative rules.
Are numismatic coins taxable in Texas?
+
Often they are exempt if they qualify as legal tender or bullion, but nonqualifying collector items can be treated differently.
Is jewelry or a gold medallion taxed in Texas?
+
Yes. Texas taxes jewelry, medallions, and accessories even though qualifying bullion and many coins are exempt.
